patch.value: Route project-schema keys to their declared flags in field refusals

Observed during SDK delivery: update with --field gate_evidence=<JSON> refuses that key as absent from active extension registrations and lists only unrelated extension fields. The same workspace declares gate_evidence as an object field with cli_flag --gate-evidence; schema show-field and update contracts expose it, and the dedicated flag succeeds. Extend field recovery to distinguish configured project-schema fields from extension item fields and provide the executable declared CLI/SDK route. Preserve extension-field admission and no-write refusals. This is a recovery/discovery gap, not a request to bypass schema validation or reinterpret arbitrary extension fields.

A rejected configured schema key names its declared CLI flag and supported SDK route; Unknown extension and reserved core keys retain distinct typed recovery; Native refused-call tests prove unchanged documents/history and execute the advertised correction
An agent can repair the rejected schema-field call using only its refusal and the actual declared field contract.
The gate_evidence refusal names only unrelated active extension fields, while contracts and schema show-field reveal the successful --gate-evidence route.

value.text:
Implementation: parseRegisteredItemFieldAssignments takes an optional project-schema resolver (createSchemaFieldRecoveryResolver in src/sdk/lifecycle/core-field-recovery.ts, wired by both create and update). A --field key the project schema declares (by key or metadata_key, through the registry's own normalizer) is refused with project_schema_field_requires_declared_flag and changed:false. The refusal carries recovery.suggested_flags with the declared flag, next steps naming the CLI flag, the SDK option (the camelCase name Commander derives from that flag, which the SDK also reads) and pm schema show-field. A key declared for other commands only says so. Unknown keys keep extension_item_field_unknown and reserved core keys keep core_item_field_requires_dedicated_flag.

CLI executability: src/cli/runtime/field-route-retry.ts rewrites exactly one matching --field key=value (or --field=key=value) token in the caller's own invocation into --<flag> value and attaches suggested_retry and suggested_retry_args. Duplicate assignments, assignments after --, a dangling --field and bare keys keep the producer recovery rather than guess.

Proof: the update-command spec refuses through the SDK with byte-identical item and history files, then executes the advertised SDK route (reviewUrl) successfully. Resolver/parser and retry-repair specs cover every branch.

patch.value: The SDK refusal leaves item and history bytes unchanged and the advertised SDK route succeeds; unknown and core keys keep their own codes.
An agent repairs a --field gate_evidence call from the refusal alone, without a write.

parseRegisteredItemFieldAssignments takes a project-schema resolver used by create and update; the refusal project_schema_field_requires_declared_flag names the flag, SDK option and schema show-field; the CLI rewrites the one matching --field token into an executable retry.

value.text: Codex review round 1 on PR #1649: the advertised SDK option for a dotted cli_flag (review.url) was the dotted spelling, which readRuntimeFieldOptionValue never reads. runtimeFieldSdkOptionName (core/schema/runtime-field-values.ts) now derives it with the same normalizer the reader uses (reviewUrl), with a regression case in extensions-item-fields.spec.ts.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 2 on PR #1649: with --review-url and --review.url both declared, the advertised SDK option (reviewUrl) would set both fields. runtimeFieldSdkOptionName now returns the first option name the reader accepts for this field that no other declared field accepts (camelCase of the flag preferred, then key-derived), and the hint is omitted when every name is shared. The spec runs collectRuntimeUpdateFieldValues with each advertised option and asserts that exactly the intended field is set.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: CodeRabbit full review on PR #1649 (head f7e12f69b): when several schema declarations share a metadata_key, the resolver now routes through one whose commands include the current command (create-only and update-only declarations both sharing triage resolve to the update one for update). docs/EXTENSIONS.md now states the lookup order: extension declarations are matched first, and only names no active extension declares reach the schema routing.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Codex review round 3 on PR #1649: two findings, both fixed.
- The advertised CLI flag could be as ambiguous as the SDK option: --x-y parses to xY, which another field's x.y flag also reads.
- A schema field with cli_flag title produced an SDK hint (title) that also set the core title.
runtimeFieldCliFlagRoute now picks the declared flag or an alias that is not a host flag and whose parsed name no other field and no host option reads. runtimeFieldSdkOptionName also excludes host option names: update/create option contracts plus global flags. A route is advertised only when it sets the field alone; otherwise the refusal says to give the field a distinct cli_flag, and no executable retry is offered.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
CodeRabbit review of 6f3d87ab7 on PR #1649: two findings, both fixed.
- Commander stores a dotted flag under its literal key (--review.url parses to options["review.url"]), which the runtime reader never checked, so such a flag silently set nothing. This was a pre-existing reader defect that the new routing could advertise. resolveCandidateOptionKeys now also reads Commander's real key for the declared flag and each alias, and the CLI route judges ambiguity by that key.
- Option ambiguity is now computed by definition identity rather than metadata_key, so two declarations sharing a storage key still count as distinct readers.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Codex review round 4 on PR #1649: three findings, all fixed.
- Negating flags: Commander files --no-title values under title. commanderOptionAttribute now strips no-, so the route and the host reservation see the real key. The runtime reader deliberately does not read a negated spelling, since that key belongs to another option.
- Incomplete host reservation: options registered directly in register-mutation (force, clear-tests, replace-tests and others) were missing. The reservation now uses the command's full flag contract (resolveSubcommandFlagContractsForCommand) plus global flags, registration targets and the SDK-only update keys (documentAnnotationSnapshot, runtimeFieldCommands, typed against UpdateCommandOptions).
- Ambiguity scope: competing fields are limited to those active for the command, so a create-only field no longer suppresses a valid update route.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Codex review round 5 on PR #1649: two findings, both fixed.
- A negated spelling (cli_flag no-review) could be advertised although the reader never reads its value, which Commander files under review, so following it did nothing. Negating spellings are no longer routes.
- A short alias (-r) chosen because the primary flag is host-owned was rendered ---r. runtimeFieldFlagToken keeps a short alias's single dash, commanderOptionAttribute strips leading dashes before computing the key (-r maps to r), and the host reservation now includes the command's short flags.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Codex review round 6 on PR #1649: two findings, both fixed.
- Host short flags live in contract.short, not aliases, so -t (--title) was not reserved and could be advertised. The host reservation now includes every contract's short flag.
- Reader precedence: readRuntimeFieldOptionValue returns the first candidate key present, so a route whose key the reader checks only after a key that a host option or another field's flag can set (alias heading after title, or review.url after reviewUrl) is shadowed whenever both appear in one invocation. CLI routes and SDK hints now require that no earlier-read key of the field is host- or field-settable (isUnshadowedOptionKey); otherwise nothing executable is advertised.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 11 on PR #1649: collectRuntimeUpdateFieldValues keeps the first value per metadata_key, so a later declaration sharing a storage key with an earlier active one is shadowed whenever both are supplied. Routes and SDK hints for such a later declaration are now withheld (hasEarlierStorageTwin); the earlier declaration keeps its own.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 12 on PR #1649: the storage-twin rule assumed first-write-wins, but the collectors differ (update keeps the first value per metadata_key, create the last), so on create the earlier declaration's route could be silently overridden. Rather than model per-command precedence, routes and SDK hints are now withheld for every declaration that shares its storage key with another declaration active for the same command (hasStorageTwin). That is safe in both directions, and covered for create and update.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 13 on PR #1649: the host reservation missed ownershipMetadataBypass and ownershipDependencyBypass, internal update keys that no flag declares. normalizeUpdateOptions clobbers a CLI value for them, and an SDK true activates an ownership bypass. Both are now reserved. hostOwnedOptions is exported, and a spec pins the reservation to every key that normalizeUpdateOptions and normalizeCreateOptions write, so a future internal key cannot be missed silently.

value.text: PR #1649 CodeRabbit round on 3b61b351a, two findings. (1) Bulk scope: update-many rows ran the schema-field resolver under the update scope, so an update_many-only field was told update cannot set it. The resolver now takes the invoking scope (from runtimeFieldCommands) and reserves update-many's host options as the union of the update row surface and the update-many flag contracts. Text names pm update-many and the update options of the update-many request. (2) Conflicting retry: pm update --field gate_evidence=new --gate-evidence old rewrote into two values for one flag, and the later one wins. Fixed producer-side, not by scanning argv in the CLI: the resolver reads the invocation options with readRuntimeFieldOptionValue, the reader the mutation itself uses. So any declared flag, alias or SDK option (including a storage twin in scope) withholds suggested_flags. The CLI then builds no retry, and the refusal says the invocation already sets the field. Specs: extensions-item-fields (bulk scope, twins, create/update/update_many) and update-command (runUpdateMany row message, alias conflict leaves the item unchanged).
